title: Fpqc schematic cover of a flat group space over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities, without assuming commutativity. Suppose $G\to S$ is separated, flat and locally of finite type: its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and flatness and local finite type are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There is an fpqc morphism of schemes $p:T\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that the sheaf fibre product $G_T=G\times_ST$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is represented, as a group sheaf, by a separated flat $T$-group scheme locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No quasi-compactness or smoothness of $G$ is assumed, and $T$ is not required to be Noetherian or of finite type over $S$.

source.place: Anantharaman, Schemas en groupes, espaces homogenes et espaces algebriques sur une base de dimension 1, Memoires SMF 33 (1973), 3.4.1, printed p.52 (OCR renders 3.4.1 as 5.4.1), including the normalization-in-an-algebraic-closure cover; local finite presentation and flatness are retained under base change. Local archive WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ and an etale scheme chart meeting the identity in the special fibre. Such a chart exists by the surjective atlas in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the hypotheses on $G$, every etale scheme chart is flat and locally of finite type over $S$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes these charts locally Noetherian; thus $G$ is locally Noetherian. By [pqf-def-locnoeth], refine the chart near a point over the identity to a Noetherian affine chart $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $(\pi)$ is proper in $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] supplies a prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $(\pi)$. By [lem-sfb-krull-principal-ideal-height-bound], $\dim A_{\mathfrak q}\leq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-schematic-near-height-one] to this chart point: there is a scheme open $U\subset G$ with $U_s\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus; algebra.tex Tag 00KV, algebra-lemma-minimal-over-1. The special fibre is nonempty because of the identity section.

proof.text: The scheme $U\to S$ is flat and locally of finite type by the chartwise hypotheses. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] on affine opens of $U$ to make it locally of finite presentation: finitely many polynomial relations suffice over the Noetherian ring $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] its image is open in $S$. It contains $s$, so it equals $S$, since an open subset of a trait containing its closed point also contains the generic point. In particular both $U_s$ and $U_\eta$ are nonempty. The same finite-presentation argument applies to every affine etale chart of $G$.

source.place: Tags 01TX (locally finite type over a locally Noetherian base is locally of finite presentation) and 01UA (flat locally finitely presented morphisms are universally open).

proof.text: Take $B,T$ from [lem-sfb-trait-absolute-normalization-local-sections], and put $H=G\times_ST$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $H$ is an algebraic space, the original atlas pulls back to an etale scheme atlas, and $U_T$ is a scheme. On each original affine chart $Y_i\to S$, step 2 gives finite presentation (the map is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Apply the base-change clauses of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] to these charts: their pullbacks are flat and finitely presented over $T$. They prove chartwise flatness and local finite presentation of $H$. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] $H\to T$ remains separated. The group operations and identities pull back as maps and equations of sheaves. For each $t\in T$, $U_t$ is nonempty: it is the scalar extension of $U_s$ or $U_\eta$, and a nonempty affine piece remains nonzero after a field extension (a basis vector survives tensoring). The point description in the normalization lemma makes all $\kappa(t)$ algebraically closed.

source.place: Tags 03MO and 03XR, base change of flatness and finite presentation; Tag 03KL, base change of separatedness; Anantharaman 3.4.1 normalization cover.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$ over $s$, and put $k=\kappa(t)$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], the nonempty locally finite type $k$-scheme $U_t$ has a $k$-point $u$. Let $x$ be any $k$-point of $H_t$ and form $g=xu^{-1}$ in the group $H_t(k)$. Pulling the etale atlas back to $g:\operatorname{Spec}k\to H_t$ gives a nonempty etale $k$-scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. It has a closed point, hence a $k$-point by the same two field-scheme lemmas; etaleness includes local finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus $g$ lifts to a $k$-point $y$ of some $(Y_i)_t$. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-absolute-normalization-local-sections] to the original flat locally finite type $R$-scheme $Y_i$ and this $y$. Its local section, followed by the atlas, gives $h:W\to H$ over an open neighborhood $W$ of $t$, with $h_t=g$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, quasi-sections as refined in the normalization lemma; varieties.tex Tag 0478; algebra.tex Tag 00FV. Anantharaman 3.4.1, lifting chart quasi-sections.

proof.text: On $H_W$, left multiplication by $h$ is an automorphism: multiplication by the section $h^{-1}$ is its inverse, by the group identities on every scheme test. Hence the translate $hU_W$ is a scheme open of $H_W$, containing $x$ because $h_tu=(xu^{-1})u=x$. It is also a scheme open of $H$: for every scheme test $D\to H$, first restrict to the open $D\times_TW$, then take the inverse image of $U_W$ under multiplication by $h^{-1}$; this is an open subscheme of $D$. This verifies representability and openness directly, without any descent of schemes. Thus every rational point in every special fibre lies in a scheme open of $H$.

source.place: Inherited trait-group helper below proof (3); elementary group translation and open-subfunctor scheme tests.

proof.text: The generic open $D(\pi)\subset T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\overline K$ by [lem-sfb-trait-absolute-normalization-local-sections]. The nonempty scheme $U_{\overline K}$ has a rational point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. For any $\overline K$-point $x$ of $H_{\overline K}$, translation by $xu^{-1}\in H(\overline K)$ sends this scheme open to a scheme open containing $x$. These are also opens of $H$, since the entire generic fibre is open. This treats generic points without asserting that an arbitrary generic group point extends to a section over $T$.

source.place: Absolute-normalization generic open; field-point existence from varieties.tex Tag 0478 and algebra.tex Tag 00FV; elementary group translation.

proof.text: Let $L\subset H$ be the largest scheme open from [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open]; it contains all scheme opens from steps 5 and 6. For each $t\in T$ pull $L_t$ back to each scheme of an etale atlas of $H_t$. Every closed point of that scheme is $\kappa(t)$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so its image lies in $L_t$. The closed complement is therefore empty by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]. Atlas surjectivity and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] give $L_t=H_t$. Every point of $H$ lies over some $t\in T$ and lifts to its fibre: the point fibre-product surjectivity in that same calculus, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, gives such a lift. Thus $L$ has full point image, so $L=H$. Therefore $H$ is represented by a scheme. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] its sheaf group operations uniquely come from scheme morphisms, and faithfulness gives their identities; this gives a group scheme without commutativity. Step 3 gives its separatedness, flatness and local finite presentation, and the normalization lemma gives the required fpqc $T\to S$.

source.place: Tag 03JH, lemma-subscheme; Tags 03H4 and 03BZ, point fibre products and equality of open subspaces; varieties.tex Tag 0478.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q30-9fc97ac17 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and both new nodes, and checked them against the cited node statements and the sources. This is not a re-split: the base item had no proof, and its statement is unchanged. The seven steps are sound. Step 1: a prime minimal over (π) in a Noetherian affine chart through e(s) has height ≤1, and the new 0ADD node gives a scheme open U with U_s nonempty. Step 2: U is flat and lfp, so its image is open, which gives U_η nonempty. Step 3: the base-change uses of flat-proper-fp-locality and separated-fp-composition apply only to affine charts over an affine base, which is honest. Step 4: a rational point u of U_t exists by the Jacobson lemma plus the residue-field lemma; g=xu⁻¹ lifts to a k-point of a chart, and the new section node gives h:W→H with h_t=g. Step 5: the translate hU_W is a scheme open containing x, and representability is written out. Step 6: the generic open is Spec K̄ and is handled separately. Step 7: L is the largest schematic open; Jacobson on lft atlases gives L_t=H_t, point calculus gives L=H, and Yoneda transfers the group law. New node lem-sfb-space-schematic-near-height-one equals Stacks 0ADD (spaces-over-fields lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus): separated, locally Noetherian, local-ring dimension ≤1 at a chart point. It is not a duplicate: lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme is global over a field, and the 0ABI groupoid node is only an input. New node lem-sfb-trait-absolute-normalization-local-sections is true. B is flat and surjective, its points are 0 or maximal, B[1/π]=K̄, and its residue fields are algebraically closed. For the local sections: flatness gives a generization, a dominant quasi-finite component through y0 gives a valuation ring of K̄ extending R, Galois transitivity plus surjectivity of the decomposition group onto Aut(κ(t)/k) moves it to the prescribed t and embedding, and finite presentation spreads the map to D(b). Small cases checked: R[x]/(x²−π) works; the non-flat R[x]/(πx) shows the flatness hypothesis is necessary. Batch-5: every sec-trace-formula node in the closures of the flagged citations lies in unit sk-i-curve-zero or sk-lem-finite (algebraic-space foundations). None is a trace-formula or Poincaré-duality step, so the citations are accepted.
